findings.message:
[P2] Refresh rotated sessions on error responses

Token rotation happens inside `hubSessionFromRequest` before the route finishes, so the old token is already deleted when this success-path code attaches the replacement cookie. If any later store or static-file access throws, the catch returns 500 without the refresh cookie and the browser keeps the invalidated token, forcing a logout after a transient backend failure. Apply the stored refresh cookie to the error response as well.

src/passport.ts:2761-2766

[P3] Make concurrent refresh expiry expectation deterministic

`refreshed.expiresAt` is built from a second `Date.now()` call, while `getHubSessionByToken` normalizes the expiry to `lastUsedAt + hubSessionIdleTimeoutMs`. If the clock ticks between those calls, the actual value is earlier than expected and the equality assertion fails intermittently. Capture one timestamp and derive both `lastUsedAt` and `expiresAt` from it.

src/store_test.ts:756-757

summary: The change implements absolute and idle session expiry plus token rotation, but the refresh cookie is only sent on the success path and the concurrent refresh test has a timestamp-dependent assertion.

evidence: src/auth_config.ts:120-121 sets hubSessionTtlMs to 30 days and adds hubSessionIdleTimeoutMs at 7 days.
src/auth_store.ts createHubSession records absoluteExpiresAt, and normalizedHubSession rejects sessions at the absolute or idle deadline.
src/auth_store.ts renewal caps expiresAt at absoluteExpiresAt, rotates the token, and atomically deletes the old key.
src/handler_test.ts and src/store_test.ts cover token rotation, idle expiry, and rejection after the absolute deadline.
